US Chemicals Industry Posts Steady Growth Amid Stable Demand in First Quarter

The US chemicals industry reported moderate growth in the first quarter, buoyed by steady demand across key sectors and resilient domestic manufacturing activity. According to figures released Tuesday by the American Chemical Producers Association, industry-wide revenues climbed 2.7% from the previous quarter to $158.2 billion, with specialty chemicals and industrial gases leading gains.

"The first three months of the year have shown that US chemical production remains robust, supported by solid buying from the automotive, construction, and consumer goods sectors," said Diane Cartwright, chief economist at the association. "We are seeing healthy inventory levels and a balanced supply chain, which has contributed to stable pricing and output."

Among the industry’s top performers, Foresight Chemicals posted a 4.3% year-on-year increase in quarterly revenue, citing strong demand for its specialty polymers used in packaging and electronics. Meanwhile, Northshore Petrochemicals reported a 2% uptick in sales, driven by increased orders from the paints and coatings segment.

Operating margins across the sector held steady at 12.5%, as lower feedstock prices partially offset higher logistics costs. "Input costs have been relatively benign so far this year, though ongoing infrastructure spending continues to put some upward pressure on transportation expenses," noted Matthew Li, a chemicals sector analyst at Wilshire Advisory.

Exports of US chemicals rose 1.8% during the quarter, with shipments to Mexico and Canada accounting for nearly half of all overseas sales. "Trade flows remain healthy, reflecting stable demand in North American markets," said Cartwright.

Employment in the chemicals industry was unchanged at 880,000, with companies reporting little difficulty in filling vacancies. The outlook from industry leaders remains cautiously optimistic, with expectations of continued gradual growth supported by steady industrial activity and favorable economic conditions.

"Given current trends, we anticipate a stable operating environment over the coming quarters," said Foresight Chemicals CEO Lila Mendoza. "Our focus remains on innovation and operational efficiency to drive long-term success."
